newsitem.title: USA: Montana Colstrip 700 MW unit restarting, at 90 MW.
newsitem.headline: Montana Colstrip 700 MW unit restarting, at 90 MW.

text.p: As expected, the 700 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant near Billings, Mont., was restarted Thursday morning, sources familiar with the plant's operations said.
The unit had reached an operating rate of 90 MW and was expected to attain full capacity by late afternoon, they said.
The unit was shut Tuesday morning due to a tube leak.
Colstrip's other units, two at 330 MW and another at 700 MW, were said to be operating normally.
Montana Power Co is the operator of Colstrip unit 4 and is responsible for the sale of 30 percent of its power output under long-term contracts.

Equity owners include Puget Sound Power and Light Co, Washington Water Power Co, Portland General Electric Co, Pacific Power and Light, and a consortium of GE Credit, Shell Oil Co and a lease-back company.
